title: [Spec] Define core architecture
body:
## Overview

Define the core architecture for the Hoshi desktop pet application. This is the foundational layer that all other features build upon — the module boundaries, data flow, and structural decisions that keep the codebase maintainable as features accumulate.

## Requirements

### Module Structure

- [ ] Define a clear separation between **main process** (Electron backend, system tray, file I/O, state persistence) and **renderer process** (UI, animations, user interaction)
- [ ] Define a **shared** module for types, constants, and utilities used by both processes
- [ ] Define a **state management** layer that owns the single source of truth for pet state (mood, needs, stats)
- [ ] Define an **IPC communication layer** with typed message contracts between main and renderer
- [ ] Define a **plugin/extension architecture** for future features (minigames, seasonal events, etc.)

### Data Flow

- [ ] Unidirectional data flow: state changes originate in the state manager, propagate to renderer via IPC, renderer renders
- [ ] No direct renderer-to-renderer or main-to-main communication bypassing the state manager
- [ ] All state mutations go through a single `dispatch` function (action → reducer → new state → notify subscribers)

### File Organization

- [ ] `src/main/` — Electron main process (app lifecycle, tray, window, IPC handlers, storage)
- [ ] `src/renderer/` — Electron renderer process (UI components, animations, interaction handlers)
- [ ] `src/shared/` — Shared types, constants, utilities, IPC contracts
- [ ] `src/state/` — State management (reducer, actions, selectors, middleware)
- [ ] `tests/` — Unit and integration tests mirroring `src/` structure
- [ ] `docs/` — Architecture decision records, coding standards, feature specs

### Technology Choices

- [ ] Document why Electron (cross-platform, web tech, system tray, transparent windows)
- [ ] Document TypeScript choice (type safety across IPC boundary, Google style guide alignment)
- [ ] Document state management approach (lightweight reducer pattern vs. Redux/Zustand — pick one and justify)
- [ ] Document testing framework (Vitest for unit, Playwright for e2e)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` exists with module diagram, data flow diagram, and technology justification
- [ ] `src/` directory structure created with placeholder files for each module
- [ ] `src/shared/types.ts` — Core TypeScript interfaces for Pet, Mood, Needs, State
- [ ] `src/shared/ipc-contracts.ts` — Typed IPC message definitions
- [ ] `src/state/pet-reducer.ts` — Pet state reducer with basic actions (FEED, PLAY, CLEAN, TICK)
- [ ] `tests/unit/pet-reducer.test.ts` — Unit tests for state reducer
- [ ] All code follows `docs/coding-standards.md`
- [ ] PR reviewed and merged

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` — Full architecture document with diagrams
- [ ] `src/main/app.ts` — App lifecycle placeholder
- [ ] `src/main/tray.ts` — Tray placeholder
- [ ] `src/main/ipc.ts` — IPC handler placeholders
- [ ] `src/renderer/index.ts` — Renderer entry point
- [ ] `src/shared/types.ts` — Core TypeScript interfaces
- [ ] `src/shared/ipc-contracts.ts` — IPC message contracts
- [ ] `src/state/pet-reducer.ts` — State reducer
- [ ] `src/state/pet-actions.ts` — Action creators
- [ ] `src/state/pet-selectors.ts` — State selectors
- [ ] `tests/unit/pet-reducer.test.ts` — Reducer unit tests
- [ ] `tests/unit/pet-actions.test.ts` — Action unit tests
- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified
- [ ] PR reviewed and merged
